name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.249.0 — Command files state their steps and point at their scripts (specs/20261008/02): the thirteen /spec command files lose every paragraph that restated what a script, driver or hook already enforces — each becomes a one-line pointer at the enforcer — plus the init.md profiling and content-bar guidance nothing pinned; numbered steps, checks, headings and every declared invocation survive. Commands shrink from 2,560 to 1,884 lines; read-load.test.js pins a per-command own-file ceiling and lowers every BUDGET entry to the measured load; the genesis command cap tightens from 120 to 84. 7.248.0 — Doctrine states contracts and points at its enforcers: the six doctrine files shrink to the contracts only prose can carry (core 337→229, genesis 797→447, mocks, design, both stage files), every rule a script or hook enforces becomes a one-line pointer at it, headings stay frozen; /spec:connect loads four scoped sections instead of the whole doctrine; every command's read-load and every doctrine file's length is now pinned at its measured value. 7.247.0 — 7.247.0: two defects the blind reviewer found in direct fixes landed without review — merge-back create --spec canonicalises an absolute spec path like the root, so a project behind a symlink no longer refuses a committed spec; expire-tests --apply counts a trimmed root-level test file as surviving, so a {testDirs} gate runs instead of being skipped with a false warning.
